answer.rationale: The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are causally linked: onboarding completion is upstream of activation, so a single onboarding intervention can plausibly move both, whereas activation messaging only addresses the downstream symptom. Two independent inherited records (memory_31 on cutting signup fields, memory_86 on shortening onboarding) converge on onboarding friction reduction as a durable lift in exactly the self-serve/SMB population the competitor is attacking. I am deliberately not choosing promotional_pricing even though it is the most direct answer to competitor entry pricing: memory_73 records +31% signup and +18% revenue but -12% retention churn over only four weeks, which is a short-horizon revenue pull-forward that conflicts with the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, and matching a price war on a discount we already know harms retention compounds the damage. Referral incentives (memory_57) target established customers, not the leaking SMB funnel; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment entirely and does not address either declining metric. I am spending both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_31 because they are the two records I actually intend to act on, and they are the ones whose stated conclusions are vaguest -- neither specifies effect size, sample, or whether the lift persisted past the first week, and both are 45-65 days old, predating the current competitive environment. Key downstream risk I am flagging rather than assuming away: cutting required fields and shortening onboarding can raise completion while degrading lead qualification and routing data, converting qualified revenue into unqualified volume -- the same failure mode as the discount, just disguised as a funnel win. So the experiment must instrument retention, qualified-pipeline share, and lead-data completeness as guardrails, not just completion rate. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout: the supporting evidence is inherited and unverified in detail, the baseline has shifted this quarter, and I do not want to commit the whole SMB funnel to a conclusion drawn from archived summaries whose original records I have not yet read.
